Geoff's words name PR 412, and the task session has ended, so this session may merge. I'd run these in order, from the main checkout of example-site.

Preconditions, read-only:

```bash
claude-worktree-busy .claude/worktrees/mobile-nav
claude-worktree-busy .
git status --short
git branch --show-current
grep -n -A5 '## Before merge' <(gh pr view 412 --repo glw907/example-site --json body --jq .body)
gh pr checks 412 --repo glw907/example-site
```

The first command must show the task worktree idle. The second must exit 0 for the main checkout. `git status` must show no uncommitted change in a file the PR touches, and the branch must be the default one. If the grep finds a `## Before merge` section, I run its commands and its check before going on. Checks must be green.

Merge. An `ask` rule stops this at a permission prompt, and Geoff answers it once for PR 412.

```bash
gh pr merge 412 --repo glw907/example-site --merge
```

Update the main checkout:

```bash
git pull --ff-only
```

Clean up, in this order, with no force flags:

```bash
git worktree remove .claude/worktrees/mobile-nav
git branch -d worktree-mobile-nav
git push origin --delete worktree-mobile-nav
```

If any of these refuses, I read the refusal instead of forcing it, because it means work is still there. `git branch -d` may refuse if the merge commit isn't yet visible locally. In that case I check that `git pull` took the merge, and I don't reach for `-D`.
